idea: Office repurposing and conversion economics research
buyer: Real estate funds and lenders holding secondary offices
pain: Stranded office assets: convert, retrofit or sell, and nobody can model the choice
v1: A conversion feasibility and economics study for one asset
verdict: Acute, current, expensive problem needing exactly her two domains; among the strongest here.

why.distribution: Warm real estate fund and lender contacts holding exactly these assets.
why.demand: Stranded offices are a live, expensive, board-level problem right now - close to a paid substitute existing.
why.fmf: Conversion feasibility requires architectural judgement and investment modelling simultaneously.
why.revenue_structure: Asset by asset, though owners hold many assets.
why.defensibility: Accumulated conversion precedents compound into genuine expertise.
why.leverage: Each asset needs her judgement on site.
why.tailwind: The office repricing cycle is forcing these decisions across the market now.

ceiling_arithmetic: £14k x 14 asset studies = £196k gross, negligible direct cost. Fourteen studies is near full-time; part-time realistic is 5-7 = £70-98k. Portfolio owners with many stranded assets could raise the per-client count.
carries: One of only two ideas scoring 4 on demand: the pain is current, expensive and unavoidable for the asset owner.
kills: Leverage. It is asset-by-asset consulting, so her calendar caps the year.
test: Ask three funds or lenders holding secondary offices what they plan to do with them.
test_pass: One asks her to study a specific building.
test_fail: They say they are waiting for the market to turn.
